source: ACGME Ophthalmic Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery Milestones 2.0

level_1: Identifies need for orbital surgery and develops a treatment plan for a simple orbital surgery case, with assistance
Develops a treatment plan for moderately complex orbital surgery
Performs critical aspects of surgical management for routine post- operative care and complications of orbital surgery
level_2: Manages care of straightforward orbital surgery patients, with assistance
Performs critical aspects of moderately complex orbital surgery (e.g., orbital decompression)

level_3: Develops a treatment plan for a routine orbital surgery case
Identifies and formulates a plan for surgical management of post- operative care and complications of orbital surgery
Performs critical aspects of complex revision or multi-disciplinary orbital surgery
level_4: Performs critical aspects of simple orbital surgery (e.g., anterior orbitotomy, orbital blow out fracture repair with implant)
Develops a treatment plan for a complex or multi-disciplinary orbital surgery
Performs critical aspects of the surgical management for post- operative care and complications of complex revision or multidisciplinary orbital surgery
level_5: Manages routine post- operative care and complications
Performs critical aspects of complex orbital surgery (e.g., lateral orbitotomy, intraconal tumor removal)

Performs critical aspects of moderately complex lacrimal surgery
Performs critical aspects of surgical management for more complex post-operative care and complications of lacrimal surgery

Develops a treatment plan for innovative lacrimal surgery
level_4: Performs critical aspects of straight forward lacrimal surgery
Develops a treatment plan for complex and/or multi-disciplinary or endoscopic sinus DCR surgery and/or high-risk
Performs and adopts innovative lacrimal surgery techniques to improve outcomes
level_5: Manages routine post- operative care and complications of lacrimal surgery
DCR surgery (e.g., post radiation or chemotherapy)
Contributes to multi- disciplinary and inter- disciplinary teams to improve outcomes for surgical procedures involving the lacrimal apparatus

level_1: Identifies the need for various types of eyelid surgery and develops a treatment plan for straightforward eyelid surgery cases
Develops a treatment plan for moderately complex eyelid surgery (e.g., eyelid sharing reconstruction, large defects, complex aesthetic unit surgery)
Performs critical aspects of surgical management for more complex post-operative care and complications of surgical procedures involving the eyelid/face
level_2: Manages care of straightforward eyelid surgery (e.g., tumors, malposition, congenital anomalies), with assistance
Performs critical aspects of moderately complex eyelid surgical procedures
Develops a treatment plan for innovative eyelid surgery
level_3: Develops a treatment plan for specific eyelid procedures and discusses indications and alternative surgical procedures for various conditions

level_4: Performs critical aspects of routine eyelid surgical procedures
Develops a treatment plan for complex and/or multi-disciplinary management or revision surgery for eyelid conditions (e.g., large periocular flaps, cervicofacial flaps, vascular pedicle flaps)
Contributes to multi- disciplinary and inter- disciplinary teams to improve outcomes in patients with surgical procedures involving the eyelid/face
level_5: Manages routine post- operative care and complications of eyelid surgery
Performs critical aspects of complex revision or multi-unit reconstruction involving eyelid/face/forehead

level_1: Identifies the need for minor aesthetic procedures, such as
Manages routine post- operative care and complications for minor periocular aesthetic procedures
Performs critical aspects of complex aesthetic oculofacial surgery
level_2: Botox and neuromodulators
Develops a treatment plan for moderately complex oculofacial aesthetic surgery (e.g., endoscopic brow lifts and lower lid blepharoplasty)
Performs critical aspects of surgical management for routine post- operative complications of complex aesthetic oculofacial surgery
level_3: Manages care of straightforward minor aesthetic procedures (e.g., Botox, fillers, chemical peels)

Develops a treatment plan for complex aesthetic revision or oculofacial surgery beyond the orbit (e.g., rhinoplasty, neck liposuction)
level_4: Develops a treatment plan for routine aesthetic procedures
Identifies and formulates a plan for surgical management of post- operative complications of periocular aesthetic surgery of moderate complexity

level_1: Demonstrates essential knowledge of eyelid, orbital, and lacrimal anatomy
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of the anatomic and pathophysiologic changes of commonly diagnosed oculofacial disorders (e.g., ptosis, entropion, ectropion)
level_3: Demonstrates essential knowledge of facial, nasal, sinus, head, and neck anatomy and pathophysiology as they relate to the orbit and adnexa
level_4: Demonstrates knowledge of complex anatomy and pathophysiology as they relate to oculofacial disorders
level_5: Publishes original research on anatomy and pathophysiology in a peer-review journal

level_1: Identifies resources to generate a focused differential for common oculofacial disorder (e.g., eyelid, orbital, lacrimal)
Articulates the rationale for ordering diagnostic testing in hierarchical fashion based on a probabilistic differential
level_2: Generates a basic differential diagnosis based on patient symptoms and history
Generates a probabilistic differential diagnosis in patients with multiple ocular and medical comorbidities; modifies likely differential with new information from additional testing
level_3: Generates a comprehensive differential diagnosis based on patient symptoms and history
Independently interprets diagnostic testing
level_4: Selects additional diagnostic testing to distinguish between conditions on the differential
Recognizes, self-reflects on, and shares experiences to educate others on factors that contributed to a missed diagnosis or faulty clinical reasoning (e.g., publication, curriculum development)
level_5: Generates refined differential based on patient symptoms, history, and examination findings, distinguishing between common and uncommon conditions

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of common patient safety events
Describes local quality improvement initiatives (e.g., eye protection for high-risk activities, diabetic eye screening)
Discloses patient safety events to patients and their families (simulated or actual)
level_2: Demonstrates knowledge of how to report patient safety events
Participates in analysis of patient safety events (simulated or actual)
Demonstrates the skills required to identify, develop, implement, and analyze a quality improvement project
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of basic quality improvement methodologies and metrics
Participates in disclosure of patient safety events to patients and their families (simulated or actual)
Actively engages teams and processes to modify systems to prevent patient safety events
level_4: Identifies system factors that lead to patient safety events
Participates in local quality improvement initiatives
Role models or mentors others in the disclosure of patient safety events
level_5: Reports patient safety events through institutional reporting systems (simulated or actual)
Conducts analysis of patient safety events and offers error prevention strategies (simulated or actual)
Creates, implements, and assesses quality improvement initiatives at the institutional or community level

level_1: Demonstrates knowledge of care coordination
Demonstrates knowledge of the local population and community health needs
Advocates for safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs within and across health care delivery systems
level_2: Identifies key elements for safe and effective transitions of care and hand-offs
Coordinates care of patients in complex clinical situations effectively using the roles of their interprofessional teams
Uses local resources effectively to meet the needs of a patient population and community
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of the role of the physician in addressing community health needs
Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in complex clinical situations
Analyzes the process of care coordination and leads in the design and implementation of improvements
level_4: Coordinates care of patients in routine clinical situations effectively using the roles of the interprofessional team members
Identifies specific local health needs related to oculoplastic care
Improves quality of transitions of care within and across health care delivery systems to optimize patient outcomes
level_5: Performs safe and effective transitions of care/hand-offs in routine clinical situations

subcompetencies.name: Physician Role in Health Care Systems

level_1: Describes basic health care systems and access models (e.g., government, private, public, uninsured care)
Describes knowledge domains for effective transition to practice (e.g., information technology, legal, billing and coding)
level_2: Demonstrates use of the electronic health record
Advocates for patient care needs beyond patients’ available resources (e.g., community resources, patient assistance resources, telehealth)
level_3: Describes how different system types require the physician to deliver care effectively with available resources
Demonstrates administrative knowledge needed for transition to practice (e.g., contract negotiations, malpractice insurance, government regulation, compliance)
level_4: Identifies the documentation required for billing and coding compliance
Participates in health policy advocacy activities
level_5: Optimizes patient care given available resources
Analyzes individual practice patterns and professional requirements in preparation for practice

level_1: Demonstrates how to access and use available evidence and incorporate patient preferences and values to care for a routine patient
level_2: Articulates clinical questions and elicits patient preferences and values to guide evidence- based care
level_3: Locates and applies the best available evidence, integrated with patient preference, to the care of complex patients
level_4: Critically appraises and applies evidence even in the face of uncertainty and conflicting evidence to guide care, tailored to the individual patient
level_5: Coaches others to critically appraise and apply evidence for complex patients, and/or participates in the development of patient care guidelines

subcompetencies.name: Reflective Practice and Commitment to Personal Growth

level_1: Accepts responsibility for personal and professional development by establishing goals; actively seeks opportunities to improve
Analyzes, reflects on, and institutes behavioral change(s) to narrow the gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
level_2: Identifies the factors that contribute to gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Uses performance data to measure the effectiveness of the learning plan and, when necessary, improves it
level_3: Demonstrates openness to performance data (feedback and other input) to inform goals; designs and implements a learning plan, with guidance
Challenges assumptions and considers alternatives in narrowing the gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
level_4: Analyzes and reflects on the factors that contribute to gap(s) between expectations and actual performance
Facilitates the design and implementation of learning plans for others
level_5: Seeks performance data and accepts it with responsibility and equipoise; demonstrates implementation of a learning plan
Coaches others on reflective practice

level_1: Identifies and describes potential triggers for professionalism lapses
Analyzes straightforward situations using ethical principles
Recognizes and uses appropriate resources for managing and resolving ethical dilemmas as needed (e.g., ethics consultations, literature review, risk management/legal consultation)
level_2: Describes when and how to appropriately report professionalism lapses, including strategies for addressing common barriers
Demonstrates professional behavior in complex or stressful situations
Coaches others when their behavior fails to meet professional expectations
level_3: Demonstrates knowledge of the ethical principles underlying informed consent, surrogate decision making, advance directives, confidentiality, error disclosure, stewardship of limited resources, and related topics
Recognizes the need to seek help in managing and resolving complex ethical situations
Identifies and seeks to address system-level factors that induce or exacerbate ethical problems or impede their resolution
level_4: Demonstrates insight into professional behavior in routine situations
Analyzes complex situations using ethical principles
level_5: Takes responsibility for one’s own professionalism lapses
Recognizes situations that may trigger professionalism lapses and intervenes to prevent lapses in oneself and others

level_1: Takes responsibility for failure to complete tasks and responsibilities, identifies potential contributing factors, and describes strategies for ensuring timely task completion in the future
Recognizes detrimental consequences when tasks and responsibilities are not completed in a timely manner (e.g., team members, compliance)
level_2: Responds promptly to requests or reminders to complete tasks and responsibilities
Recognizes situations that may impact others’ ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
level_3: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with attention to detail in routine situations
Proactively implements strategies to ensure that the needs of patients, teams, and systems are met
level_4: Recognizes situations that may impact one’s own ability to complete tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner
Takes ownership of system outcomes and attempts to implement changes at a systems level to advance the goals of professional accountability
level_5: Performs tasks and responsibilities in a timely manner with attention to detail in complex or stressful situations
